leads.question: Can the preserved SPC set fingerprint the audio driver, song table, sample/instrument layout, and reachability of the two tagged unused songs?
leads.next_discriminator: Causally reconstruct the two evidence-backed unused-song load pairs with the fail-closed counterfactual patcher: block 0x3B while retaining Demo package 03:FB15, and block 0x3D while retaining race package 03:FB55. Compare the resulting APU transfer bytes/state against the preserved unused-song SPCs. Continue 0x3C caller/delta archaeology only where it helps explain the near-twin 0x3B/0x3C relationship.
deliverables: SPC archive provenance, archive hash and ten per-track hashes (landed)
shared APU driver/sample fingerprint and reusable analyzer (landed)
Unused Song 1 classified with Demo Race; Unused Song 2 classified with numbered-race family (landed)
CPU-side APU transfer boundaries corrected: initializer 02:8298, wrapper 02:82A5, body 02:82A9; exact first-race APU block $B0E0-$BDE0 mapping (landed)
first-race ROM source seed 03:FB55 plus clustered sibling seeds identified and runtime-corroborated (landed)
six selector tables mapped to 12 exact direct callers; FB95 has no direct caller and is FAD5 minus blocks 07/15/29 (landed)
unused-song ROM records identified: $3B=Unused Song 1, $3D=Unused Song 2; both absent from exact immediate upload-call corpus (landed)
blocks 07/15/29 correlated against SPC corpus: 29=Demo/Unused1, 07=Celebration, 15=all tracks (landed)
retail setup-selector map landed; $3B/$3D are the only absent values in $38-$42 (landed)
direct $3B/$3D reachability closed: 36/36 wrapper calls immediate-ID, zero $3B/$3D LDX, no alternate inner-body caller (landed)
full 0x00..0x31 package-block/SPC signatures reproduce known package mappings and attribute Unused Song 1 to reused 03:FB15, Unused Song 2 to reused 03:FB55 (landed)

leads.question: Which detailed player-reported mechanics in cabbagery's 2024 recollection are accurate, and which can be promoted into durable behavioral fixtures or subsystem documentation?
leads.next_discriminator: Reproduce the claims independently against the canonical ROM/runtime in small slices: (1) enumerate Hunter path-crossing effects and trigger behavior; (2) verify Hunter unlock propagation into 2P/versus/league and whose progression state gates it; (3) verify top-three record persistence and identity/color mutation after overwriting a racer; (4) characterize stunt scoring on Downer and adjacent stunt courses using deterministic inputs; (5) map rejected-name behavior to the existing forbidden-name evidence; (6) verify Anti-Uni/Neon endgame gating. Promote only locally reproduced facts.
deliverables: Hunter crossing-effect behavior matrix with deterministic reproduction
record-orphaning fixture covering racer overwrite and retained record value
bounded stunt-scoring characterization for Downer plus one comparison course
forbidden-name cross-check against existing ROM/achievement/patch evidence
promoted symbols/tests/docs only for confirmed claims
leads.acquisition_judgment: High-value because the claims are concrete and cheaply falsifiable. Do not treat recollection as authority; use it to seed canonical-ROM/runtime experiments.

leads.question: Which community-documented mechanics recur across independent sources strongly enough to justify direct canonical-ROM/runtime tests and durable fixtures?
leads.next_discriminator: Prioritize independently repeated, implementation-relevant claims: stunt score values/decay, boost gain and offscreen depletion, track-color cue semantics, Hunter/Anti-Uni effect triggers, screen-position/scrolling influence on race timing, Mega stunt detection, and rejected-name substring behavior. For each claim, build the cheapest deterministic reproduction and record corroborating versus conflicting sources before promotion. Also verify TAS-reported Tabletop duration-dependent scoring and whether airborne stunt input remains active after the stunt timer reaches zero. Treat Tabletop as an explicit exception to the usual repeat-score halving rule and verify repeated identical-duration Tabletop scores.
deliverables: source conflict notes where player recollections disagree
Tabletop duration-scoring and stunt-timer overrun fixture
course-video timing/screen-state sanity checks for Zoom Zoo, Bowl, Switcher and Monster
leads.acquisition_judgment: High leverage because multiple independent player/research communities describe overlapping mechanics; canonical reproduction can turn folklore into durable regression tests cheaply.

leads.question: How do already-confirmed stunt-message boost rewards translate into racer speed over time, especially across landing quality, airborne storage, offscreen depletion and the 0x0180 boost clamp?
leads.next_discriminator: Do not re-derive the stunt-message reward path: Nitrodon's recovered disassembly already confirms queued message consumption adds per-message boost to persistent P1/P2 boost state, and the current-player boost workspace/offscreen decrement/clamp paths are already mapped. Use deterministic same-state traces only to resolve the remaining game-facing relationship between boost units and speed: compare representative low/high reward stunts, clean versus poor landings, onscreen versus offscreen depletion, airborne storage, and approach to the 0x0180 clamp. Align the trace with the recovered message-consumer reward frame.
deliverables: landing-quality effect separated from boost reward
leads.acquisition_judgment: High value because independent experienced-player sources disagree on a core racing mechanic. Cheap deterministic measurement should settle it.

leads.question: Which malformed SRAM states can reproduce historically reported name, score, palette, or startup corruption, and how should the modern host/profile layer fail safely around them?
leads.next_discriminator: Use known SRAM structure and existing profile/save tooling to generate bounded corruptions around racer identity, score tables, and nearby metadata. Reproduce only project-owned synthetic cases; do not assume the forum-reported battery/root-cause theory. Verify stock behavior where practical, then ensure modern Windows profile handling detects or contains malformed state without silently damaging unrelated profiles.
deliverables: stock-behavior observations for recoverable corruption classes
explicit separation of observed symptoms from unproven hardware/root-cause claims
leads.acquisition_judgment: Useful because it turns real historical failure symptoms into bounded robustness tests for the modern save/profile layer.

leads.question: How does the stock red/yellow off-course recovery track work, and which collision/state transitions allow the player to enter, traverse, bypass, or escape it?
leads.next_discriminator: Treat the manual as primary intent evidence: red/yellow track is deliberately laid down to prevent unicycles falling forever when they are far off the normal course. Reproduce the three player-described escape families on canonical runtime: vertical-jump floor penetration, seat-impact escape at recovery-track arrows, and turnaround-zone bypass. Capture course position, collision mode, track-piece identity, camera/screen state, waypoint state and finishability before/after each transition. Distinguish intended recovery geometry from bugs that let the player bypass or corrupt it.
deliverables: reproducible input traces for each confirmed escape family
collision/state transition trace across normal -> fallback -> normal or broken state
fixture for at least one recoverable escape and one non-finishable/corrupted path if canonical behavior confirms them
documentation separating player terminology from engine-confirmed semantics
manual-intent cross-check for red/yellow recovery geometry
leads.acquisition_judgment: High-value because the source describes concrete, reproducible geometry escapes that can expose hidden recovery-track and collision-state semantics.

leads.question: How exactly does the stock handicap/rubberband system depend on racer separation, screen position, opponent class, and circuit/race mode?
leads.next_discriminator: Use deterministic traces that intentionally fall behind then recover, measuring racer speed/boost, opponent state, screen-X position and lap time against matched no-handicap controls. Reproduce the historical strategy of letting Bronzen get ahead for unusually fast circuit laps and distinguish player handicap from camera/scroll effects.
deliverables: interaction with screen position and scrolling
validated or rejected historical low-time strategy
leads.acquisition_judgment: Core racing behavior repeatedly mentioned by competitive players and reviews; inexpensive deterministic measurement can resolve it.

leads.question: Which stock persistence/UI invariants are violated or intentionally tolerated by player-discovered medal-selection and league-deletion edge cases?

deliverables: modern host compatibility decision for each stock edge state
leads.acquisition_judgment: High product relevance because both claims touch persistence and profile semantics now being modernized.

leads.question: How does twist-derived boost interact with twist-track sections that punish or redirect jumping, and is the resulting friction purely level design or tied to distinct track-state rules?
leads.next_discriminator: Use the 2026 original-developer thread's player recollection as a design-friction lead. Identify twist-track sections where jumping is disadvantageous or causes rollback, then compare grounded twist-track traversal against jump-and-twist traversal while tracing boost, position, rollback/recovery state and camera. Do not infer intended design rationale beyond observable behavior.
deliverables: classification as level-design constraint versus distinct track-state mechanic
leads.acquisition_judgment: Useful because it connects a remembered player pain point to specific track-state and boost behavior already under investigation.

leads.question: What exact input/state rules permit simultaneous roll-twist and flip-twist recognition, including flat-ground starts, buffered inputs, landing-angle misclassification, and turbo-controller claims?
leads.next_discriminator: Reproduce the TAS-thread techniques on canonical runtime: roll-twist by holding roll while releasing twist after one completed twist; back-forward twist input without the twist button; flip-twist variants; and the reported case where exact landing orientation credits a roll as a flip. Compare normal controller timing to high-frequency/turbo-style input without assuming turbo is required.
leads.acquisition_judgment: High leverage because several experienced players independently describe subtle input/state behavior that directly affects movement, scoring and speed.

acquisition_policy.rule: Keep all leads searchable, but do not let low marginal-value artifacts block implementation or reverse engineering.

tiers.P0: active hunt; likely to materially reduce implementation uncertainty
tiers.P1: useful corroboration; pursue opportunistically or with cheap automation
tiers.P2: optional evidence; acquire if easy, never block
tiers.P3: archival tail; preserve lead, no bespoke recovery effort unless a new discriminator raises its value

deduplication_policy.rule: Before adding a new external-evidence lead, search the research ledger, reference notes, catalog, generated analysis surfaces and current worklist for the same artifact, mechanic, course/glitch, address, or behavioral question under alternate terminology.

statuses.corroboration_only: New source supports an already solved fact; add provenance to the existing source set but do not create a new work item.
statuses.discriminator_only: New source adds a genuinely new test or conflicting claim; extend the existing work item.
statuses.new_lead: Create a work item only when the repository lacks both the fact and a suitable active discriminator.
